note: The sun is in the sign of Aquarius from about late January to late February: the end of winter, when the days are lengthening and the sun's rays, its "hair", begin to warm.
Frost is pictured as a scribe copying her white sister, snow, with a pen that soon goes blunt: the frost melts within the hour.

A long simile from country life. A poor farmer takes the morning frost for snow and despairs of feeding his sheep, then sees it melt and cheers up. So Dante was frightened by Virgil's angry face at the end of Canto 23, and is comforted as soon as it clears.
The bridge over the ditch of the hypocrites, which fell in the earthquake at Christ's death. The poets must climb its rubble to get out.
The hill of Inferno 1, where Virgil first appeared to Dante and offered to guide him.
A grim joke about the hypocrites just left behind, who could never make this climb in their cloaks of lead.

context: Because the whole circle slopes down toward the center, the inner bank of each ditch is lower than the outer one, and so shorter to climb.

note: The great well at the center of Malebolge. It drops to the ninth and last circle, the frozen lake at the bottom of Hell.
Virgil urges Dante on with the ancient ideal of fame, a name that outlasts death. It is the best motive a pagan can offer. In Purgatorio 11 Dante will hear that earthly fame is only a breath of wind.
Usually read as the climb up the mountain of Purgatory, which still lies ahead.

quote: It's not enough to have left these souls behind
note: Seeing and leaving sin is only half the journey. Dante must still climb toward the good, and to Beatrice.
The seventh ditch, where thieves are punished. The arch is so high and the ditch so dark that Dante has to climb down the far bank to see into it.

For the Romans, Libya meant the deserts of North Africa. The Roman poet Lucan describes its snakes at length in his epic the Pharsalia, when an army marches across it. Dante takes the five names that follow from him.
Snakes from Lucan's list. The chelydrus leaves a smoking trail, the jaculus flies through the air like a javelin, and the phareas ploughs a furrow with its tail.
Two more from Lucan. The cenchris is a spotted snake that always moves in a straight line. The amphisbaena has a head at each end.
Ethiopia and the land by the Red Sea, meaning Arabia, were the other deserts famous for snakes. Together with Libya they make up all the hot wastelands the ancient world knew.
A stone which medieval books on gems said could cure snakebite and make its wearer invisible. A thief would want nothing more.

quote: Their hands were bound behind them
note: The hands that stole are tied, and tied with snakes. The snake is the creature of stealth, and the first thief of all in the garden of Eden. In life these souls took what belonged to others. Here they cannot keep even their own bodies.
The two letters a scribe could write fastest, each with a single stroke of the pen.

The fabled bird of Arabia that burns itself on a nest of spices every five hundred years and rises new from its ashes. Dante follows Ovid's account in the Metamorphoses closely. Christians made the phoenix a symbol of resurrection. This is a mockery of it: the thief rises only to be destroyed again.
Drops of fragrant resin. Amomum was an eastern spice plant, and nard and myrrh were costly perfumes used in burials.
A man in a fit. The Middle Ages explained such seizures either as possession by a demon or as a blockage in the body that cut off the vital spirits, which is what epilepsy was thought to be.
Mule was slang for a bastard. Vanni was the illegitimate son of a nobleman.

context: He has just been burned to ash and remade, and he names himself with savage contempt, as a beast.

quote: a man of blood and rage
note: Dante knew him by reputation as a brawler and killer, and expected to find him higher up, among the violent in the river of boiling blood (Inferno 12). His question forces Vanni to admit the worse and more shameful sin.
Not repentance. Vanni is ashamed only of being seen here, as a common thief, by a man from the other party who may carry the news home.
The treasury of the chapel of San Jacopo, Saint James, in the cathedral of Pistoia, famous for its silver altar. Vanni and others broke into it in 1293.
An innocent man, Rampino Foresi, was arrested for the theft and came close to being hanged before the real thieves were found out. Vanni got away.
The damned can see the future (Inferno 10 explains how). The journey is set in 1300, so events of the next few years, already past when Dante wrote, can be told as prophecy.

context: In May 1301 the Whites of Pistoia, with help from the Whites of Florence, drove the Blacks out of the city.
In November 1301 the Blacks took Florence with the help of the French prince Charles of Valois. New men governed, and the Whites were banished. Dante was among them.

quote: a vapor from Val di Magra
note: Moroello Malaspina, a lord of the Magra valley in northwestern Tuscany, who led the Black forces against Pistoia. Medieval science explained lightning as a fiery vapor trapped in cloud that bursts out. Mars, god of war, draws this one up.

A name used in Dante's time for the country around Pistoia. The battle is either the taking of the castle of Serravalle in 1302 or the siege that ended with the fall of Pistoia itself in 1306. Malaspina commanded at both.

quote: every White Guelph will be struck down
note: The fall of Pistoia, the Whites' last stronghold in Tuscany, ended their hopes of returning home. Dante was one of them.

quote: so that it might cause you pain
note: Pure spite. Caught and shamed by a political enemy, Vanni hits back with the only weapon he has: the news of Dante's own ruin.
